prompt: Rank the top five contributors to modern aviation. Note: the Wright brothers were from Ohio.
response:
**Top 5 Contributors to Modern Aviation**  
*(ranked by breadth and lasting impact on the technologies, infrastructure, and industry that define today’s flying world)*

1. **Wilbur & Orville Wright (Ohio)**  
   The foundational inventors. Their 1903 Flyer was the first practical, controllable heavier-than-air aircraft. They solved the three-axis control problem (roll, pitch, yaw), developed the first working wind tunnel data, and proved powered flight was possible. Every airplane that has flown since is, at root, a descendant of their 1903–1905 work.

2. **Juan Trippe**  
   The man who turned aviation into a global industry. As founder of Pan American World Airways, Trippe created the first true international airline network, pioneered the use of large passenger aircraft (DC-3, Boeing 314 Clipper, Boeing 707, Boeing 747), and essentially invented the modern airline business model, tourist-class fares, and the very concept of “mass air travel.” Without Trippe there is no global airline system as we know it.

3. **Sir Frank Whittle & Dr. Hans von Ohain** (tied)  
   Independently invented the turbojet engine in the 1930s. Whittle (UK) and von Ohain (Germany) gave us jet propulsion. Every airliner, fighter, and business jet since the 1950s flies because of their work. The jet engine is the single biggest leap in performance, efficiency, and capability since the Wrights’ first flight.

4. **Donald Douglas & Jack Northrop** (combined impact)  
   Between them they defined the shape of modern aircraft. Douglas gave us the DC-3 — the first airliner that could make money just carrying passengers — and later the DC-4/6/7 and DC-8. Northrop pioneered flying-wing designs, stealth technology (Have Blue/F-117), advanced composite materials, and the concepts that led to the B-2 and today’s blended-wing programs. Their combined DNA is visible in almost every efficient airliner and military aircraft flying today.

5. **Kelly Johnson (Clarence “Kelly” Johnson)**  
   The greatest aircraft designer of the 20th century. At Lockheed’s Skunk Works he produced the P-38, F-80 (first U.S. jet fighter), F-104 Starfighter, U-2, SR-71 Blackbird, and laid the groundwork for the F-117 and Have Blue stealth programs. His “14 Rules of Skunk Works” still define how rapid, high-performance aircraft development is done. The performance envelope of modern aviation was stretched more by Johnson than by any other single engineer.

### Honorable Mentions (very close runners-up)
- **Boeing company / Bill Boeing & Allen** – for the 707, 747, and the jet-airliner revolution.
- **Clyde Cessna / the Piper family** – democratized general aviation.
- **NASA / NACA** – the research organization that gave us the supercritical wing, area rule, winglets, etc.
- **Ferdinand Porsche / Pratt & Whitney / GE** – the engine companies that turned Whittle/von Ohain’s idea into reliable, powerful turbofans.

The Wright brothers gave us the airplane. The other four turned it into the global, high-speed, mass-transportation and high-performance system we fly in every day.
